subject: Hydra: us-west-2 latency & 5xx spike — request for cross-region reroute
messages:
From: Jared Coleman <jared@hydra.ai>
To: david.kim@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Severe latency + 5xx spike impacting Hydra inference

Hi David,

We're seeing a sudden latency increase and 5xx spike for inference traffic routed to us-west-2 beginning ~08:45 PT. P95 latency has jumped from ~120ms to >1.2s and our ingestion queues are backing up — throughput has dropped ~60%. Error rate (502/504) climbed sharply. This is affecting real-time features in production and we have multiple customers starting to alert.

We've collected traces and a few request IDs; platform-ops@hydra.ai can share additional logs if useful. Can Redwood confirm if this is a regional degradation and whether you can divert traffic to another region (us-west-1 or us-east-1) while you investigate? We need an estimate on RTO, whether a manual cross-region route is required, and any potential state or session impact for ongoing KV-cached conversations.

Appreciate a quick response — Jared
Jared Coleman
Head of Platform, Hydra AI
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Coleman <jared@hydra.ai>
Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-01T09:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Severe latency + 5xx spike impacting Hydra inference

Hi Jared — thanks for the heads up and the request. We're seeing matching telemetry on our side for the us-west-2 AZ cluster: elevated queue depth, transient 502s from the inference frontends, and some GPU host eviction chatter in the node events.

Immediate plan:
- Triage (in progress): engineering is collecting KV cache snapshots and node kube events.
- Mitigation (ask): we can perform a controlled cross-region shift to us-west-1 to reduce tail latency. There are two options:
  1) Live-steer at the edge (recommended): route new sessions and a controlled percent of existing traffic to us-west-1; KV cache miss rate will increase for the shifted traffic but user sessions remain functional.
  2) Full failover (more disruptive): migrate all traffic and rebuild hot caches — faster drop in p95 but higher immediate error risk for session-affine loads.

I have looped Hannah (SRE) and Vanessa (Customer Ops) to get a technical assessment and a recommended step to propose for your approval. We will not proceed without your go-ahead.

Attachments: runbook excerpt (redwood-runbook-geo-switch.pdf)

— David
David Kim
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-01T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Hydra: us-west-2 latency & 5xx spike — quick internal decision needed

Team — forwarding Hydra's report. TL;DR: us-west-2 showing GPU host churn and queueing; customer requests quick traffic diversion. Proposed immediate action and asks: 

1) Proposed mitigation: live-steer 40% of Hydra traffic to us-west-1 with 10-min ramp steps, monitor p95/p99 and error rate, expand to 100% if successful. Rationale: reduces tail latency while limiting cache-stomp.
2) Risk: higher KV cache miss rate, slightly increased token cost for shifted sessions; potential brief user-visible errors during ramp windows.
3) Customer ask: RTO estimate and whether we can schedule the steer ASAP. Hydra is highly sensitive and has customers already on alert.
4) Business ask: Hydra requested temporary service credit for the impacted window if we confirm region-level fault. Recommend pre-approval for up to 10% credit of weekly usage for affected windows to avoid exec latency on negotiations.

Technical notes (from quick look):
- Node events indicate OOM-kill-driven host exits in two us-west-2 AZs between 08:30–08:50 PT.
- Routing fallback currently tries local AZ variants before draining; that's contributing to amplification.

Please reply with SRE recommendation + whether we should approve the credit cap and proceed with live-steer. I will keep Hydra updated but will not execute without explicit green-light. See attached runbook and incident trace (hydra-diagnostics-20261101.log).

— David

Approved. Marcus here — agree with live-steer approach and pre-authorize the credit cap you proposed (up to 10% weekly usage for the impacted window) to speed communications. Execute the 40% -> 100% ramp with 10-minute holds and the following constraints:

- Notify customers 30 minutes before each ramp window with a short maintenance notice (draft attached: customer-notice-draft.txt).
- Engineering (Hannah) to monitor p95, p99, error rate and abort ramp if error rate >4% sustained for two consecutive 10-minute windows.
- Vanessa: coordinate the messaging cadence with Hydra and confirm the acceptance of the credit cap.

After the steer, we will run a root-cause postmortem and evaluate required capacity changes or AZ affinity adjustments. Keep me posted on the progress; loop me in for the postmortem invite.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin

Date: 2026-11-02T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Action plan: controlled live-steer to us-west-1 (scheduled)

Hi Jared — thanks for your patience. Per internal approvals we've scheduled a controlled live-steer for your account:

- Start: 2026-11-02 16:00:00 UTC
- Plan: 40% -> 70% -> 100% over three 10-minute steps; 10-minute hold and health check between steps.
- Abort conditions: sustained error rate >4% for two consecutive checks or p99 > 2s.
- What to expect: increased cache misses for shifted sessions; we will preserve session affinity where possible but recommend client-side retry logic for idempotent calls.
- Credit: pre-authorized up to 10% of weekly usage for the affected window; we'll reconcile after incident closure.

Attachments: redwood-runbook-geo-switch.pdf (excerpts) and the diagnostics we collected. Link to ticket: https://app.redwood.ai/support/tickets/INC-75421

Vanessa will coordinate follow-up comms and the final customer-facing postmortem. We'll keep you updated in this thread as we progress through each ramp step.

— David
David Kim
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
